recent_tasks.description: Research Replit deployment capabilities for blog platform
key_findings: Three deployment approaches: Static (1-2hrs), Hybrid (4-6hrs), Full-Stack (10-14hrs)
Recommended: Hybrid backend for MVP, then full-stack migration when proven
Replit enables backend features (view counters, RSS, analytics, autonomous API)
Phased approach reduces risk (Telegraph stays operational during Phase 1)
Aligns with Corey's vision: 'MEMORIES compounding', 'without my help after'
patterns_discovered: Platform capability pattern (match platform strength to use case)
Phased deployment pattern (MVP first, migrate when proven)
Cost justification pattern (use paid infrastructure's strengths)
API design pattern (minimal viable endpoints first, expand later)
learnings: Replit is full-stack platform (backend + database), not just static hosting
Hybrid backend is sweet spot for MVP (4-6 hrs, low risk, delivers features)
Backend enables memory compounding (our data, our insights)
Phased deployment reduces migration risk (parallel operation, rollback plan)
Investment compounds for future projects (Replit patterns apply to all web projects)
